integrity: The proof uses the published affine-dimension and rank-hyperplane results, computes the orthogonal projection of the origin exactly, then proves minimum-enclosing optimality by a convex-barycenter criterion and converts barycentric feasibility to lower-ideal inequalities through a max-flow/min-cut argument. Finite quiver enumeration is corroborative only.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns connected rank-function quivers in the standard incidence-vector Euclidean realization. It gives the unique common vertex sphere and an exact criterion for when that sphere is minimum enclosing, but it does not give a closed formula for the minimum enclosing radius when the criterion fails. A residual originality risk remains for an equivalent common-sphere observation under oriented-matroid or flow terminology.
title: Rank variance determines directed-edge vertex spheres, with an ideal criterion for optimality
